title: Keyboard Manager shortcut editor does not identify a key

status.label: Identify the unrecognized shortcut key
status.detail: The report says a key appears as undefined and prevents creating distinct tool shortcuts, but gives no version, key, or reproduction steps.

judgment.rationale: The issue describes a possible Keyboard Manager shortcut-editor failure but does not identify the key displayed as undefined, the attempted mapping, the PowerToys version, or the Windows/input layout. The text also asks for a more usable editor, so the exact failure must be separated from a general UX request before proposing a fix.
evidence: The report says the shortcut editor recognizes an undefined key and prevents distinct shortcuts for tools.
No PowerToys version, Windows version, exact key combination, keyboard layout, steps, or follow-up are recorded.
The issue is open, unassigned, and labeled Issue-Bug and Area-User Interface.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact key and mapping, current PowerToys/Windows versions, keyboard layout, and a short reproduction; do not repeat or expose the contact detail embedded in the original title.

fix_assessment.rationale: If a supported key is consistently represented as undefined in the shortcut editor, the capture or display path may fail to identify it. The report is too sparse to identify the key or distinguish a capture defect from unsupported hardware.

proposed_fixes.title: Display captured shortcut keys accurately
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The editor may not map a captured key event to a displayable key identity, or the reported key may be unsupported by the current input path. No key or layout is specified.
plan: Collect the exact key, mapping, PowerToys and Windows versions, and keyboard layout.
Reproduce capture in the shortcut editor and trace the captured key identity through display and persistence.
Correct the mapping or provide an explicit supported/unsupported-key explanation.
Add a focused editor test for the reported key and layout.
verification: Verify the reported key is displayed consistently when captured and after reopening the mapping.
Verify the editor accepts distinct valid shortcuts for the tools in question.

confidence.rationale: The report suggests an editor issue, but no concrete key, version, or reproduction is available.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says Keyboard Manager shows an undefined key in the shortcut editor, preventing distinct tool shortcuts, and asks for a different editing approach.
known_information: The issue is labeled Issue-Bug and Area-User Interface and names Keyboard Manager.
The report has no version, exact shortcut, keyboard layout, reproduction steps, comments, or attachments.
inferences: The undefined-key symptom may reflect key capture or display handling, but the report does not establish that it is a product defect rather than an unsupported key or an editor usability concern.
issue_context.analysis: The next useful step is a focused clarification. Avoid designing a replacement editor or proposing a code path before the unrecognized key and attempted mapping are known.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, labels, state, and available discussion.
No linked fix or related issue was identified.

information_gaps.information: The exact key and shortcut being entered, the displayed undefined value, PowerToys and Windows versions, and the active keyboard layout
information_gaps.why_needed: These details determine whether the editor fails to identify a supported key or whether the behavior is a layout/unsupported-key limitation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Open the Keyboard Manager shortcut editor, reproduce the capture, and report the key combination, the value shown for the key, PowerToys and Windows versions, and keyboard layout; a screenshot of the editor is useful if available.

comment.body: Could you share the exact key combination you are trying to assign and what the editor displays as “undefined”? Please include your PowerToys and Windows versions and keyboard layout, and a screenshot of the shortcut editor if possible. That will help distinguish a key-capture problem from an unsupported key or a request for a different editor workflow.
